meta.title: A Small Arithmetic Dataflow
meta.subtitle: Explore how two inputs propagate through reusable operations

learning_outcomes.description: Trace how changing either input changes several deterministic arithmetic results.

sections.title: Inputs and derived quantities
sections.paper_explanation: This synthetic example defines two scalar inputs and derives their sum, difference, product, and ratio.
sections.simple_explanation: Change either number and follow the same value through several operations.

boundaries.description: The second input stays above zero so the displayed ratio is defined.

sections.title: Explore the arithmetic flow
sections.paper_explanation: The computation graph applies only registry operations and executes them in declared order.
sections.simple_explanation: The charts and values below always read the latest browser-side computation results.

guided_explorations.title: Change the left input
guided_explorations.instruction: Enter a new left value while holding the right value fixed.
guided_explorations.observe: Compare how the sum, difference, product, and ratio respond.
guided_explorations.explanation: Every result depends on the left input through a different registry operation.

guided_explorations.title: Move the right slider
guided_explorations.instruction: Move the right value across its range.
guided_explorations.observe: Watch the bars, line, pipeline, and intermediate values update together.
guided_explorations.explanation: All visual components resolve their values from the same recomputed context.

boundaries.description: This is a deterministic arithmetic demonstration, not a scientific model.

concepts.name: Numeric dataflow
concepts.summary: Shared inputs feed several deterministic operations and displays.

assessment.prompt: If the left input increases by one, how does the sum change when the right input stays fixed?
assessment.explanation: The sum is the left input plus the fixed right input.
